798 |   /**
799 |    * Parse `argv`, setting options and invoking commands when defined.
800 |    *
801 |    * Use parseAsync instead of parse if any of your action handlers are async.
802 |    *
803 |    * Call with no parameters to parse `process.argv`. Detects Electron and special node options like `node --eval`. Easy mode!
804 |    *
805 |    * Or call with an array of strings to parse, and optionally where the user arguments start by specifying where the arguments are `from`:
806 |    * - `'node'`: default, `argv[0]` is the application and `argv[1]` is the script being run, with user arguments after that
807 |    * - `'electron'`: `argv[0]` is the application and `argv[1]` varies depending on whether the electron application is packaged
808 |    * - `'user'`: just user arguments
809 |    *
810 |    * @example
811 |    * ```

813 |    * program.parse(process.argv); // assume argv[0] is app and argv[1] is script
814 |    * program.parse(my-args, { from: 'user' }); // just user supplied arguments, nothing special about argv[0]
815 |    * ```
816 |    *
817 |    * @returns `this` command for chaining
